arxiv-2103-02510.title: Inverse design method for periodic and aperiodic metasurfaces based on the adjoint-method: metalens with random-like distributed nano-rods Journal: oe Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2103-02510.creator: Kofi Edee \authormark 1,*, Mauro Antezza \authormark 2,3, Brahim Guizal \authormark 2
arxiv-2103-02510.description: Abstract The classical adjoint-based topology optimization (TO) method, based on the use of a random continuous dielectric function as an adjoint variable distribution, is known to be one of the most efficient optimization methods that enable the design of optical devices with outstanding performances.

arxiv-2109-02295.title: Applying explicit symplectic integrator to study chaos of charged particles around magnetized Kerr black hole Journal: EPJC
arxiv-2109-02295.creator: Wei Sun 1,2, Ying Wang 1,2, Fuyao Liu 1, Xin Wu 1,2,3
arxiv-2109-02295.description: Abstract In a recent work of Wu, Wang, Sun and Liu, a second-order explicit symplectic integrator was proposed for the integrable Kerr spacetime geometry. It is still suited for simulating the nonintegrable dynamics of charged particles moving around the Kerr black hole embedded in an external magnetic field. Its successful construction is due to the contribution of a time transformation.

arxiv-2111-01583.title: Observation of topological flat bands in the kagome semiconductor Nb 3 Cl 8
arxiv-2111-01583.creator: Zhenyu Sun, Hui Zhou, Cuixiang Wang, Shiv Kumar, Daiyu Geng, Shaosheng Yue, Xin Han, Yuya Haraguchi, Kenya Shimada, Peng Cheng, Lan Chen, Youguo Shi, Kehui Wu, Sheng Meng, Baojie Feng
arxiv-2111-01583.description: Abstract I Abstract The destructive interference of wavefunctions in a kagome lattice can give rise to topological flat bands (TFBs) with a highly degenerate state of electrons. Recently, TFBs have been observed in several kagome metals, including Fe 3 Sn 2 , FeSn, CoSn, and YMn 6 Sn 6 .

arxiv-2202-14029.title: On the transmission of turbulent structures across the Earth’s Bow Shock Journal: ApJ Letters
arxiv-2202-14029.creator: Domenico Trotta, Francesco Pecora, Adriana Settino, Denise Perrone, Heli Hietala, Timothy Horbury, William Matthaeus, David Burgess, Sergio Servidio, Francesco Valentini
arxiv-2202-14029.description: Abstract Collisionless shocks and plasma turbulence are crucial ingredients for a broad range of astrophysical systems. The shock-turbulence interaction, and in particular the transmission of fully developed turbulence across the quasi-perpendicular Earth’s bow shock, is here addressed using a combination of spacecraft observations and local numerical simulations.

arxiv-2308-01297.title: The Star Formation Across Cosmic Time (SFACT) Survey. III. Spectroscopy of the Initial Catalog of Emission-Line Objects IRAF , WRALF ( Cousins 2019 ) , and ALFA ( Wesson 2016 )
arxiv-2308-01297.creator: David J. Carr, Jennifer Sieben, John J. Salzer, Samantha W. Brunker, Bryce Cousins
arxiv-2308-01297.description: Abstract The Star Formation Across Cosmic Time (SFACT) survey is a new narrow-band survey designed to detect emission-line galaxies (ELGs) and quasi-stellar objects (QSOs) over a wide range of redshifts in discrete redshift windows. The survey utilizes the WIYN 3.

arxiv-2308-06623.title: Polyp-SAM++: Can A Text Guided SAM Perform Better for Polyp Segmentation?
arxiv-2308-06623.creator: Risab Biswas
arxiv-2308-06623.description: Abstract Meta recently released SAM (Segment Anything Model) which is a general-purpose segmentation model. SAM has shown promising results in a wide variety of segmentation tasks including medical image segmentation. In the field of medical image segmentation, polyp segmentation holds a position of high importance, thus creating a model which is robust and precise is quite challenging.

arxiv-2309-11558.title: Estimating major merger rates and spin parameters ab initio via the clustering of critical events Estimating major merger rates and spin parameters ab initio via the clustering of critical events – E
arxiv-2309-11558.creator: Corentin Cadiou, Eric Pichon-Pharabod, Christophe Pichon, Dmitri Pogosyan
arxiv-2309-11558.description: Abstract We build a model to predict from first principles the properties of major mergers. We predict these from the coalescence of peaks and saddle points in the vicinity of a given larger peak, as one increases the smoothing scale in the initial linear density field as a proxy for cosmic time.

arxiv-2405-08766.title: Energy-based Hopfield Boosting for Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2405-08766.creator: Claus Hofmann, Simon Schmid, Bernhard Lehner, Daniel Klotz, Sepp Hochreiter
arxiv-2405-08766.description: Abstract Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is critical when deploying machine learning models in the real world. Outlier exposure methods, which incorporate auxiliary outlier data in the training process, can drastically improve OOD detection performance compared to approaches without advanced training strategies.

arxiv-2409-08061.title: Khintchine dichotomy for self-similar measures Thanks: W.H. is supported by the National Key R&D Program of China (No. 2022YFA1007500) and the National Natural Science Foundation of China (No. 12288201). Thanks: H.Z. is supported by the startup grant of Soochow University.
arxiv-2409-08061.creator: Timothée Bénard, Weikun He, Han Zhang
arxiv-2409-08061.description: Abstract . We extend Khintchine’s theorem to all self-similar probability measures on the real line. When specified to the case of the Hausdorff measure on the middle-thirds Cantor set, the result is already new and provides an answer to an old question of Mahler.

arxiv-2410-12961.title: Super-resolving Real-world Image Illumination Enhancement: A New Dataset and A Conditional Diffusion Model
arxiv-2410-12961.creator: Yang Liu 1,, Yaofang Liu 2,, Jinshan Pan 3, Yuxiang Hui 1, Fan Jia 1, Raymond H. Chan 4, Tieyong Zeng 1
arxiv-2410-12961.description: Abstract Most existing super-resolution methods and datasets have been developed to improve the image quality in well-lighted conditions. However, these methods do not work well in real-world low-light conditions as the images captured in such conditions lose most important information and contain significant unknown noises.

arxiv-2506-07000.title: The k k -Total Bondage Number of a Graph Journal: Discrete Mathematics
arxiv-2506-07000.creator: Jean-Pierre Appel, Gabrielle Fischberg, Kyle Kelley, Nathan Shank, Eliel Sosis
arxiv-2506-07000.description: Abstract Let G = ( V , E ) G=(V,E) be a connected, finite undirected graph. A set S ⊆ V S\subseteq V is said to be a total dominating set of G G if every vertex in V V is adjacent to some vertex in S S .

arxiv-2506-12617.title: From Human to Machine Psychology: A Conceptual Framework for Understanding Well-Being in Large Language Model s
arxiv-2506-12617.creator: Gabriel RongYang Lau, Wei Yan Low
arxiv-2506-12617.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Gabriel RongYang Lau, Wei Yan Low. As large language models (LLMs) increasingly simulate human cognition and behavior, researchers have begun to investigate their psychological properties. Yet, what it means for such models to flourish, a core construct in human well-being, remains unexplored. This paper introduces the concept of machine flourishing and proposes the PAPERS framework, a six-dimensional model derived from thematic analyses of state-of-the-art LLM responses.

arxiv-2509-24325.title: ReCon-GS: Continuum-Preserved Guassian Streaming for Fast and Compact Reconstruction of Dynamic Scenes
arxiv-2509-24325.creator: Jiaye Fu, Qiankun Gao, Chengxiang Wen, Yanmin Wu, Siwei Ma, Jiaqi Zhang, Jian Zhang
arxiv-2509-24325.description: Abstract Online free-viewpoint video (FVV) reconstruction is challenged by slow per-frame optimization, inconsistent motion estimation, and unsustainable storage demands. To address these challenges, we propose the Re configurable Con tinuum Gaussian Stream, dubbed ReCon-GS , a novel storage-aware framework that enables high-fidelity online dynamic scene reconstruction and real-time rendering.

arxiv-2602-17110.title: Grasp Synthesis Matching From Rigid To Soft Robot Grippers Using Conditional Flow Matching
arxiv-2602-17110.creator: Tanisha Parulekar, Ge Shi, Josh Pinskier, David Howard, Jen Jen Chung
arxiv-2602-17110.description: Abstract A representation gap exists between grasp synthesis for rigid and soft grippers. Anygrasp [ 5 ] and many other grasp synthesis methods are designed for rigid parallel grippers, and adapting them to soft grippers often fails to capture their unique compliant behaviors, resulting in data-intensive and inaccurate models.

pmc-11337138.title: Transforming Primary Care Data Into the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model: Development and Usability Study
pmc-11337138.creator: Mathilde Fruchart, Paul Quindroit, Chloé Jacquemont, Jean-Baptiste Beuscart, Matthieu Calafiore, Antoine Lamer, Christian Lovis
pmc-11337138.description: BackgroundPatient-monitoring software generates a large amount of data that can be reused for clinical audits and scientific research. The Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) consortium developed the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model (CDM) to standardize electronic health record data and promote large-scale observational and longitudinal research.

pmc-11641943.title: Exploring the Biological Activity of Phytocannabinoid Formulations for Skin Health Care: A Special Focus on Molecular Pathways
pmc-11641943.creator: Guilherme Trigo, Mariana Coelho, Carolina Borges Ferreira, Matteo Melosini, Inês Sousa Lehmann, Catarina P Reis, Maria Manuela Gaspar, Susana Santos, Alessandro Terrinoni
pmc-11641943.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recent advancements have highlighted the potential of cannabis and its phytocannabinoids (pCBs) in skin health applications. These compounds, through their interaction with the endocannabinoid system (ECS), show promise for skin health products. Their ability to regulate inflammation, oxidative stress and cell proliferation makes them useful in addressing skin problems such as inflammation, scarring, healing, acne and aging, positioning them as valuable tools for innovative skincare solutions.

pmc-12474344.title: A Critical Review of Bovine Viral Diarrhea Virus: Spotlights on Host Plasticity and Potential Spillover Events
pmc-12474344.creator: Eaftekhar Ahmed Rana, M. Asaduzzaman Prodhan, Joshua W. Aleri, Syeda Hasina Akter, Henry Annandale, Sam Abraham, Subir Sarker, Jully Gogoi-Tiwari, Jasim Muhammad Uddin
pmc-12474344.description: The bovine viral diarrhea virus (BVDV) infects a wide range of domestic and wild mammals. This review hypothesized that there might be cross-species transmission of BVDV. Therefore, the aim was to explore the BVDV-5′ UTR and N-pro sequence-based evidence to understand host plasticity among different animals.

pmc-12531959.title: Threat-related attentional bias in subjects with different looming cognitive styles: Evidence based on eye-tracking study
pmc-12531959.creator: Xuan Wang, Shuai Chen, Bin Tian, Wen-Peng Cai
pmc-12531959.description: BACKGROUNDAlthough extensive research has investigated attentional biases based on the looming vulnerability model of anxiety, the characteristics of attentional biases in individuals with looming cognitive styles (LCS) remain incompletely elucidated. No prior eye-tracking studies have examined the spatiotemporal dynamics of their threat-related attentional preferences.

pmc-12732350.title: Impact of CeO2-Doped Bioactive Glass on the Properties of CMC/PEG Hydrogels Intended for Wound Treatment
pmc-12732350.creator: Sofia Pacheco, Inês Alexandra Marques, Ana Salomé Pires, Maria Filomena Botelho, Sílvia Soreto Teixeira, Manuel Graça, Sílvia Gavinho
pmc-12732350.description: Diabetes mellitus is a serious public health problem, mainly due to the difficulty in healing chronic wounds, which present an inflammatory response for long periods of time and are more vulnerable to infections. Hydrogels are a promising therapeutic solution due to their biocompatibility, biodegradability, and ability to allow controlled release of therapeutic agents.

pmc-13391420.title: Intra-household gender difference in dietary diversity and its determinants in a food-insecure community in the Democratic Republic of Congo
pmc-13391420.creator: Nelly Kabena-Ngandu, Rosa Munsambe-Yambu, Josué Lukusa, Landry Egbende, Alexandre Bukasa-Kanyama, Bernard-Kennedy Nkongolo, Alain Cimuanga-Mukanya, Marie-Claire Muel Telo Muyer, Freddy Bangelesa
pmc-13391420.description: Introductionfood insecurity in the Democratic Republic of Congo affects over 25 million people, with Kasaï Oriental Province among the most impacted-approximately 74.9% of households face acute food shortages. While food access has been widely studied, evidence on intra-household, gender-based differences in dietary diversity is limited, particularly in highly food-insecure urban settings.

pmc-13427006.title: Fibrocalculous Pancreatic Diabetes: Changing Clinical Spectrum and Glycaemic Response to Pioglitazone
pmc-13427006.creator: Don David, Manjunath Goroshi, Vanishri Ganakumar, Vikrant Ghatnatti
pmc-13427006.description: Introduction:Fibrocalculous pancreatic diabetes (FCPD) is a unique form of diabetes characterised by irreversible damage to the pancreatic parenchyma with intraductal calcification, progressively leading to beta-cell damage. The classical clinical presentation of FCPD is evolving, with a declining frequency of typical phenotypes and increasing involvement of individuals with normal BMI and older age at presentation.

pmc-13524879.title: Timing of response in patients with relapsed/refractory FLT3mut+ acute myeloid leukemia treated with gilteritinib
pmc-13524879.creator: Alexander E Perl, Mark J Levis, Andrew H Wei, Hee-Je Kim, June-Won Cheong, Jian Li, Sergey Bondarenko, Hisayuki Yokoyama, Naoko Hosono, Nahla Hasabou, Dina Elsouda, Juan Ariza, Jamie Jung-Hee An, Jianxiang Wang
pmc-13524879.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Key Points•Most (89%) remitting patients achieved CRc within 6 gilteritinib cycles; more later vs early responders achieved a best response of CR.•Given the potential for delayed response, at least 6 gilteritinib cycles should be administered before determining treatment failure.

pmc-13550209.title: Transient early increase in echocardiographically estimated pulmonary artery pressure after closure of a large patent ductus arteriosus in an adult: a case report
pmc-13550209.creator: Peng Dai, Rui Xu, Yifan Yan, ZiHan Liang, Zongwei Xiao
pmc-13550209.description: Pulmonary artery pressure generally decreases after closure of a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) following elimination of abnormal left-to-right shunting. However, transient increases in echocardiographically estimated pulmonary artery pressure may occasionally occur during the early postoperative period. We report a 41-year-old woman with a large tubular PDA and echocardiographic evidence of pulmonary hypertension.
